summary: Martin Baumann is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1990–1993) and his habilitation at the University of Leipzig (~1994–1999). In 2001, he became Professor and head of the Religionswissenschaftliches Seminar at the University of Lucerne.

Martin Brauen is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1970–1972) and earned his doctorate at the University of Zurich (~1970–1979). He worked at Zurich's Ethnographic Museum (1975) and was chief curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge (~1959–1962) and Harvard (PhD 1969–1975). He taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo (1963–1969) and directed the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and completed his PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (-2002). His appointments include Hamburg, the University of Göttingen, Ryukoku University, Shandong University (2019), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Martin Haug was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. Educated at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1859–1866) and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at the University of Munich (1868).

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1909–1916) under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and served at the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He completed his MA, PhD, and habilitation at the University of Freiburg, also studying at Marburg under scholars including Eva Tichy and Helmut Rix. He served at Freiburg (~1999–2008) before joining the University of Jena in 2013.

Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology and sociology. He earned his BA at Cornell (~1960–1964) and his MA and PhD at Harvard (~1964–1971). He held faculty posts at Michigan (1970–1994) and George Washington (1994–2000), and became sociology professor emeritus at Harvard (2000).

Martin Lehnert works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg and served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

Martin Lowenthal is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Berlin, and Heidelberg (Promotion), completing his habilitation at Munich (-1990). He served as professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg (-2004) under Barend Jan Terwiel. He held an affiliation at Hamburg (attested 2004) and is attested as a Council member of the Pali Text Society (2026).

Martin Straube is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn. His appointments include positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University (PhD attested 2002 under Richard P. Hayes). He has served as an instructor at McGill University.

Martin Willson was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Lambert Schmithausen for her MA and earned her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), where she has worked as a researcher.

Martine Kropman is an Indology researcher. She conducted PhD research at the University of Groningen and is an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of Michigan under supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied with mentor Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), later serving on the faculty at the University of Michigan (~1949–1988).
Mary Anne Cartelli is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Philip Boas Yampolsky (attested 1999).
